chunks: Make fear of Allāh the routine of your life. Cover yourselves with peace of mind and clinch your teeth because this makes the sword slip off from the skull. Complete your armour and shake your swords in their sheathes before showing them out. Have your eyes on the enemy. Use your spears on both sides and strike (the enemy) with swords.
Keep in mind that you are before Allāh and in the company of the Prophet’s cousin.

key_terms.ابْنُ عَمِّ رَسُولِ اللهِ: The cousin of the Messenger of God

ai.seo_question: What are the key spiritual and military instructions given in this passage from Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage, part of Imam Ali’s (AS) military sermons, blends spiritual fortitude with practical battlefield tactics, using vivid metaphors like 'biting the knuckles' to signify intense focus and readiness. It underscores the concept of *muraqabah* (awareness of God) in combat, reminding soldiers that their actions are witnessed by the Divine and guided by the leader of the faithful. This synthesis of inner tranquility (*sakinah*) and outer discipline reflects the Shia understanding of leadership as both a spiritual and martial responsibility.
